items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: A fellow named Booker Coleman had that band. And I never will forget... They had a sound something like Jimmy Lunceford.

ctx.x: But right down under this building there was a nightclub where they had chorus girls and all of that, and they called it the Cotton Club. That was also at Tenth and U, and that featured... The band there was under the leadership of a drummer, a fellow named Tommy Miles. That was the band that just before this period I'm talking about had musicians in it like Trummy Young -- I guess he sort of had his apprenticeship in Tommy Miles' band. It also had a tenor saxophone player and arranger whose name was Jimmy Mundy.…
And down the street there was a place called the Casino. A fellow named Booker Coleman had that band. And I never will forget... They had a sound something like Jimmy Lunceford.

So there was all this music around, and I had to listen to it, and I was growing by leaps and bounds. And at this particular job where I was working, whenever these fellows got off from work... Then as now, whenever guys work in a big band, they never get enough of a chance to play, or never get to play long enough. So usually, when guys work in big bands,
